verdict.rationale: Proton Pass stores TOTP secrets alongside saved logins and documents its own backup-and-restore path: export to a PGP-encrypted ZIP, then import that file directly into Proton Pass. That gives a manual route to rebuild items, including tokens, on another device. Nothing in the evidence documents the lost-phone scenario itself (signing in on a new device and having tokens reappear), and nothing confirms the export includes TOTP secrets. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of cross-device sync or restore of TOTP tokens on a new device, account-recovery steps after device loss, confirmation that exports include 2FA secrets, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: Proton Pass can securely generate TOTP codes for websites that you have saved login details for.
If you want to use your passwords elsewhere or create a separate hardcopy, you can easily export your data from Proton Pass.
You can import a PGP-encrypted ZIP file directly into Proton Pass (see below).
